findings.evidence: Line 44: "This is the one positive-definiteness estimate behind the local shape of a finite-type diagram, and the results below are its corollaries." vs line 55 and line 310 added by this PR.

findings.issue: Module docstring still says the star bound "is the one positive-definiteness estimate behind the local shape of a finite-type diagram, and the results below are its corollaries", contradicting line 55 ("The second positive-definiteness estimate of the file removes that hypothesis") and line 310 ("the second, and last, positive-definiteness estimate of this file").

findings.evidence: Line 239 vs line 310 ("The proof is the second, and last, positive-definiteness estimate of this file") and line 503 ("By the no-triangle theorem the neighbours are automatically pairwise non-adjacent").

findings.evidence: Line 563-565 "...neither the combinatorial axioms nor the rank-two bound exclude it; ... it is `TauCeti.IsFiniteType.det_ne_zero` that rules it out"; line 287 "Equality holds exactly at `α = β = γ = 1`, the simply laced triangle, which is the affine diagram `Ã₂`"; `not_isFiniteType_doubleEdgeTriangle` (line 593) shows the identical proof shape applies.
findings.fix: Note that `apply_eq_zero_of_apply_ne_zero` also excludes it (at equality), and that `det_ne_zero` is merely the tool this proof uses.
findings.issue: `not_isFiniteType_affineA₂`'s docstring enumerates which tools fail and concludes "it is `TauCeti.IsFiniteType.det_ne_zero` that rules it out". After this PR the new no-triangle theorem also excludes Ã₂ (it is a triangle: `A 0 1 ≠ 0`, `A 0 2 ≠ 0`, `A 1 2 = -1 ≠ 0`), so the exclusivity reading is wrong — indeed line 287 identifies Ã₂ as the equality case of the triangle estimate.

summary: The new docstrings are accurate and the module docstring lists every new declaration, but two pre-existing claims that the star bound is the file's only positive-definiteness estimate were left in place and are directly contradicted by the new text, and the Ã₂ docstring's exclusivity claim is now stale.
